title: Compute-In-Memory on FPGAs for Deep Learning: A Review
problem: Deep learning acceleration on FPGAs suffers from a data movement bottleneck between memory blocks and compute units. FPGAs lack built-in compute-in-memory capabilities to mitigate this von Neumann bottleneck.
motivation: Compute-in-memory architectures can overcome memory wall limitations in deep learning accelerators, and FPGAs' reconfigurability enables exploration of diverse CIM implementations to improve performance and energy efficiency.
method: Compute-in-memory puts processing logic right inside memory blocks rather than having separate memory and processors that swap data back and forth. On FPGAs (reconfigurable chips), engineers modify the memory blocks already built into the chip to also perform calculations. Because computation happens where data lives, it eliminates the slow, energy-expensive data movement that creates a bottleneck in traditional computer designs.
key_novelty: Using existing FPGA memory blocks as the foundation for compute-in-memory, adding computation capability to what's already there instead of requiring entirely new custom hardware.
contributions: Overview of CIM and FPGA architecture motivating custom FPGA designs with CIM capability
Detailed analysis of CIM operation on FPGAs with focus on memory block modifications
Categorization of existing FPGA CIM proposals and explanation of architectural nuances
Discussion of current challenges for broader adoption of CIM on FPGAs
limitations: This is a review paper without novel experimental results or empirical comparisons; it synthesizes existing approaches and discusses challenges rather than proposing new solutions or demonstrating concrete improvements.
primary_theme: compute-in-memory for FPGA-based deep learning acceleration
